# Theirs renames (or kills, or re-keys) the admin doing the merge. The entry can
# neither be applied - the merger signs everything that follows - nor be dropped:
# git has already moved .sesam/signkeys/admin.age one-sidedly, so a merged log
# still naming "admin" would not load. The merge is refused instead.

sesam-repo

exec sesam tell --user bob --recipient $BOB_PUBKEY --group dev
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add bob'

# OURS: an unrelated change, so the audit-log driver runs at all.
exec git checkout -b ours
exec sesam user change-groups --user bob --group-add ops
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'ours: bob += ops'

# THEIRS: rename the admin who will be doing the merge.
exec git checkout -b theirs ours~1
exec sesam user rename admin boss
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'theirs: admin -> boss'

exec git checkout ours
! exec git merge theirs
stderr 'renames the merging admin admin'
stderr 'abort the merge'

# The refusal has to be reachable: the repo still loads, and aborting restores it.
exec git merge --abort
exec sesam verify
exec sesam show .sesam/audit/log.jsonl
! stdout 'boss'
